title: React Module 01 Applied Check
description: Apply the introductory React mental model to setup issues, first-component mistakes, props, composition, and simple interactivity.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A component is written as `function profileCard() { return <div />; }` and used as `<profileCard />`. What is the main problem?

options.text: The component name starts lowercase, so JSX treats it like a DOM tag
Function components cannot return div elements
JSX cannot be used in functions

questions.explanation: Custom React components should start with a capital letter, such as `ProfileCard`.

questions.prompt: You edit a Vite React app and the browser updates without a full manual refresh. What feature are you seeing?

options.text: Hot module replacement or fast refresh in development

questions.explanation: Vite development tooling updates the browser quickly as files change.

questions.prompt: Which are reasonable first checks when a new React app does not start? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Check the terminal error from `npm run dev`

questions.explanation: Setup troubleshooting starts with prerequisites, dependencies, and the actual terminal error.

questions.prompt: A `ProfileCard` component needs to display different users. Which design fits the React mental model best?

options.text: Hard-code one user inside the component
Read the user from a random global variable

questions.explanation: Props let the same component render different data while staying reusable.

questions.prompt: A React component should directly call `document.querySelector` during render to keep text in sync.
questions.explanation: Rendering should describe UI from data. Direct DOM manipulation during render works against React.

questions.prompt: What happens conceptually when state changes in a component?

options.text: React schedules a re-render so the UI can reflect the new state
React permanently mutates the JSX file

questions.explanation: State updates tell React to render again using the new state snapshot.

questions.prompt: Which examples show composition? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Passing content between opening and closing component tags
Building a page from several smaller components
Putting all UI in one giant component forever

questions.explanation: Composition means building larger UIs by combining smaller components and children.

questions.prompt:

`. What should you do?

options.text: Wrap them in one parent element or a Fragment

questions.explanation: A component must return one root value, which can be an element or Fragment.
